**73,28,1a** For Meletius, who was appointed in Antioch by Acacius’ party – for this is the origin of Acacius’ stance, so as to turn aside even a little from their heterodox opinion, and he shows himself, forsooth, among the orthodox, in order to confirm the aforesaid Meletius in his appointment.

**73,28,1b** For this Meletius, having been appointed by these very men of Acacius’ party, was thought by them to be of their own opinion, but he was not found to be so, as many report about him.

**73,28,2** For now those who are attached to him and to his faction, from the time when he was persecuted and driven from his own see, advancing with time and with the long duration of his persecution, and attaching themselves to it for God’s sake, are orthodox.

**73,28,3** For the greater part of the laity belonged to this faction, the one of the council; and they, having appointed bishops for themselves, confess admirably concerning the Son and do not reject the consubstantial, but say that they hold it in readiness, should a full council take place, to confess it and not deny it.

**73,28,4a** For it came about that this same most honourable Meletius, appointed by the Arians of Acacius’ party, gave an exposition, as a first-fruit, at his first address in the church of the Antiochenes; and, as most say, in orthodox fashion.

**73,28,4b** I shall set out his exposition here, and it is as follows.

**73,28,4c** Copy of a homily of Meletius.

**73,29,1a** The most wise Preacher says that the end of a discourse is good beyond its beginning.

**73,29,1b** Inasmuch as it is better and safer to cease from the contest of speaking than to begin it, especially when the same Preacher says, “This wisdom of the poor man is despised, and his words are not heard.”

**73,29,2a** Since the body is not a single member but many, and all the members take thought for one another, so that there may be no division within the body, and the head cannot tell the feet, “Of you I have no need,” but “God has blended the body together, giving greater honour to the part that lacks.”

**73,29,2b** That, when the whole body is moved, one cannot excuse oneself from being moved along with it, is self-evident.

**73,29,3a** But what beginning might one make of the discourse before us?

**73,29,3b** Or is it plain that, at the beginning of every word and deed, it is fitting to make peace the beginning and the end, and, beginning from it, to end in it?

**73,29,3c** For this, the apostle says, will turn out for salvation by means of your prayer and the Spirit’s supply, whom Jesus bestows on all who believe in him.

**73,29,4** And whether one speaks edification, or exhortation, or the consolation of love, or the fellowship of the Spirit, it comes about through the peace that is according to God, not indeed to all without distinction, but to the lovers of the law, as the prophet puts it: the law, not the bodily one, which has an image and shadow of the things to come, but the spiritual one, which wisely unveils the outcome of what was proclaimed beforehand.

**73,29,5a** “For great peace,” he says, “is for those who love you, and for them there is no stumbling-block,” so that it is plain that the stumbling-block remains for those who have hated peace, and that those who long to be freed from these should hold up love toward the Lord before them as a kind of shield.

**73,29,5b** “For he is our peace, who made both one and broke down the dividing wall of the fence, abolishing in his flesh the enmity, the law of commandments in ordinances.”

**73,29,6a** And neither can the Lord’s commandment be kept unless the love of God goes first.

**73,29,6b** “For if you love me,” he says, “you will keep my commandments”; nor is it possible for the eyes or the heart to be enlightened, unless the commandment enlightens them.

**73,29,6c** “For the commandment of the Lord,” he says, “is far-shining, enlightening the eyes”; but neither is it possible to put forth a word of truth unless one has Christ speaking within him, according to him who says, “If you seek a proof of the Christ who speaks in me,” or rather, who not only speaks but also shows mercy.

**73,29,7a** “For let your mercy and your salvation come upon me,” he says, “and I shall give an answer to those who reproach me.”

**73,29,7b** This would not come to be unless one seeks out the statutes.

**73,29,7c** For with those who are not so disposed, the shame that lies in reproaches rests on their outward bearing, so that they cannot say, “Remove from me reproach and contempt.”

**73,29,7d** And the word of truth is removed from the mouth, so that it is of no further avail to the one who prays, “Do not take the word of truth out of my mouth.”

**73,30,1a** And when does this happen?

**73,30,1b** When one does not keep the law continually; when one does not walk in a broad place.

**73,30,1c** The heart must be enlarged if anyone means to make room for Christ walking within – Christ whose glory is told not by men but by the heavens; for “the heavens tell the glory of God” – or rather by the Father himself, who says, “This is my Son, the beloved, in whom I am well pleased.”

**73,30,2** Him it is not possible to confess “if one speaks unrighteousness on high to his neighbour”, if one should call himself into the rank and name of the antichrists, having forsaken the Christians’ rank and name, concerning whom it is said, “Do not touch my anointed ones.”

**73,30,3a** “For who,” he says, “is the liar, but he who denies that Jesus is the Christ?”

**73,30,3b** “This,” he says, “is the antichrist.”

**73,30,3c** “For he who denies the Son does not have the Father either, but he who confesses the Son confesses the Father also.”

**73,30,3d** “What then,” he says, “you heard from the beginning, let it remain in you.”

**73,30,3e** “And if,” he says, “what you heard from the beginning remains in you, you too will remain in the Son and in the Father.”

**73,30,4a** And we shall remain when we make our confession in the presence of God and of the elect angels, and also before kings, and are not ashamed.

**73,30,4b** “For I spoke,” he says, “of your testimonies before kings, and I was not ashamed.”

**73,30,4c** That he is Son of God, God from God, One from One, Only-begotten from the Unbegotten, the choice offspring of him who begot him, and a Son worthy of him who is without beginning, the inexpressible interpreter of the inexpressible, Word and Wisdom and Power of him who is beyond wisdom and power, beyond what a tongue can utter, beyond what thought can move toward.

**73,30,5** An offspring perfect and abiding, from one perfect and abiding in sameness, not flowing out from the Father, nor cut off and divided, but come forth impassibly and entire from him who has lost nothing of what he had.

**73,30,6a** And that the Son is and is called Word, yet is not understood as a voice of the Father, nor as an utterance.

**73,30,6b** For he subsists of himself and acts, and through him are all things and in him are all things, just as also, being himself Wisdom, he is not understood as a thought of the Father, nor as a movement and activity of the ruling faculty, but as an offspring like the Father and reproducing exactly the stamp of the Father.

**73,30,7a** For “him has God the Father sealed”; and it is not that he exists in another while not subsisting of himself, but he is an active offspring, which has made this universe and always preserves it.

**73,30,7b** These things are sufficient to free us both from the error of the Greeks and from the self-made worship of the Jews and from the false belief of the heretics.

**73,31,1a** But since certain persons, perverting the sense of the words that stand in the Scriptures and interpreting them otherwise than is fitting, and understanding neither the force of the terms nor the nature of the things, dare to set aside the Godhead of the Son, stumbling at the word of creating that occurs in the Proverbs, “For the Lord created me as beginning of his ways, unto his works” – men who ought to follow the life-giving Spirit, and not the letter that kills.

**73,31,1b** For the Spirit gives life.

**73,31,2** Come then, let us too venture to treat these matters a little, not because it has not been said fully by those who have spoken before us – for one would be mad to say this – nor because you need a teacher – for you yourselves are taught by God – but that we may be made manifest in our consciences as being among those who desire to impart some spiritual gift to you.

**73,31,3** Believe, then, that neither elsewhere in Scripture nor in the present passage are the words of Scripture contrary to one another, even if they seem to conflict in the eyes of those who are not sound in the faith, or who are weak in judgement, and that none of the examples found in the world can be discovered which suffices of itself to present clearly the nature of the Only-begotten.

**73,31,4** And for this reason Scripture has used many conceptions and names concerning the Only-begotten, if somehow through what is on our level we might be able to grasp what is above us, and through what is known to form an image of what is unknown, being led on gently and little by little from the manifest to the hidden.

**73,31,5a** Since, then, it was needful that those who believe should believe in Christ, that the Son is like the Father, being indeed the image of him who is over all, he who is through all, through whom all things have been fashioned, both those in the heavens and those on earth.

**73,31,5b** But an image, not as a lifeless thing is of a living one, nor as the working of an art, nor as the product of an activity, but an offspring of him who begot him.

**73,31,6** And that it is not right for the Only-begotten’s generation, which is before the ages, to be characterized by bodily human generation; and that, after the pattern of wisdom, which comprehends human thoughts – the Father’s wisdom, however, being not without hypostasis or existence – Scripture used both words, that of creating and that of begetting, both “he created” and “he begot”, not so that contrary things should seem to be said of the same things in the same respect, but so that through “he created” it might present what is subsistent and abiding, and through “he begot” what is special and distinctive to the Only-begotten.

**73,31,7a** “I,” he says, “came forth from the Father, and I am come.”

**73,31,7b** And the name of wisdom too is sufficient to shut out every notion of passion.

**73,32,1** But where are we being carried off to, forgetful of the one who said, “O depth of riches and of wisdom of the knowledge of God! How beyond searching are his judgements, and how untraceable his ways”?

**73,32,2a** For we have as our teacher the Spirit of truth, whom the Lord gave us after his taking up into the heavens, “that we may see the things freely given to us by God, in which we also speak, not in words taught by human wisdom, but in those taught by the Spirit, comparing spiritual things with spiritual”, in whom we serve and worship.

**73,32,2b** Therefore we are dishonoured in him in whom the prophets prophesied, in whom the righteous were guided, through whom we are brought to the Son.

**73,32,2c** But why are we busying ourselves with the matters of the nature?

**73,32,2d** For are we, then, conversing as with people of the flesh, and not as with spiritual people?

**73,32,3a** For it was said in the case of others, “We cannot speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to people of the flesh.”

**73,32,3b** For there is cause to fear lest, through contentiousness over things incomprehensible and through the search into things unattainable, we fall into an abyss of impiety.

**73,32,3c** “And I said, I will become wise; and it went far from me, beyond what it was, and a deep depth: who shall find it?”

**73,32,4a** For let us remember the one who said, “In part we know and in part we were prophesying; but when the perfect has come, then what is partial will be abolished.

**73,32,4b** If anyone thinks he knows, he has not yet known as he ought to know.”

**73,32,4c** And for this reason there is cause to fear lest perhaps we be forcing ourselves to speak about things of which we are not able to speak.

**73,32,4d** For one must speak from faith, not believe from what is spoken.

**73,32,4e** For “I believed,” it says, “therefore I spoke.”

**73,32,5** When, then, unable as we are to declare anything about our own birth, we busy ourselves with curiosities and set about contending over the begetting of God, how is there not cause to fear lest he who grants not merely an instructed tongue but also the knowing of when a word ought to be spoken should condemn our rashness in speaking to silence?

**73,32,6** This is what was done in the case of the blessed Zacharias, who, since he did not believe the one who brought him the good news of the child’s birth, but put the grace and power of God to the test with human calculations, and debated with himself whether an old man has it in his nature to beget a child by a woman advanced in years — what does he say?

**73,32,7a** “How shall I know this, that it will be?

**73,32,7b** For I am an old man, and my wife is advanced in her days.”

**73,32,7c** Accordingly, when he heard, “Behold, you shall be silent and unable to speak”, he did not speak when he came out.

**73,33,1a** Therefore, ceasing to contend over things disputed and over things beyond us, we hold fast to what we have received.

**73,33,1b** For who is it that dares to be puffed up with knowledge, when the very man who was counted worthy of the revelations, “he who was taken up into the third heaven, he who heard words not to be uttered”, was chastened into sobriety by the thorn in respect of the flesh, lest he be lifted up above measure?

**73,33,2a** And the very prophet who said, “I believed, therefore I spoke; I was humbled”, says, “not merely, but exceedingly.”

**73,33,2b** For the nearer anyone seems to be to knowledge, the more he ought to reckon within himself that he is a man.

**73,33,2c** On this, hear what he says: “But I said in my ecstasy, Every man is a liar.”

**73,33,3a** Since, then, we have the teacher of truth, let us no longer make use of human teachers, but, taking thought, let us busy ourselves neither about modes nor about anything else.

**73,33,3b** For just as it is not possible to tell the begetting of the Son, so neither is it possible to declare the manner of the begetting from the Father; but one must consider this sufficient for teaching, that “all things came into being through him, and without him not even one thing came into being.”

**73,33,4** May the Lord grant that we, minded like Abraham, the one who says, “I have now begun to speak to my Lord, and I am earth and ashes”, and not exalting ourselves like the cedars of Lebanon — since it is not in words taught by human wisdom but in those taught by faith that the smooth and peaceable wisdom is attained — may not be in perplexity,

**73,33,5a** but, whatever we do, may be well-pleasing to God and the Father, and with him also to the Son together with him in the Holy Spirit, to whom be the glory, the might, the honour and the power, now and always and to the ages of ages.

**73,33,5b** Amen.

**73,33,5c** The confession of Meletius is concluded.

**73,34,1a** It seemed good to these people, the greater part of the Arians, to transfer him from the Pontic country, not to their joy nor for their relief, but to their vexation.

**73,34,1b** Thereupon they stir up the emperor and plot against the man, on the ground that he had not confessed him a perfect creature, and they thrust him out of his see.

**73,34,2** And the man is driven by night into an exile that lasts up to these present times; he is still in his own homeland, a man honoured and much loved, above all because of what we now hear he has accomplished, and because of what those under him in Antioch now confess, no longer making any mention at all, not even in passing, of the word ‘creature’, but confessing Father and Son and Holy Spirit consubstantial, three hypostases, one essence, one Godhead;

**73,34,3a** as is the true faith, the faith from of old, prophetic, evangelical and apostolic, which our fathers and bishops who assembled at the council of Nicaea confessed, in the time of Constantine, the great and most blessed emperor.

**73,34,3b** May it come about that the most honoured Meletius himself also confesses thus, like those under him in Antioch and those in certain other places who confess thus.

**73,34,4** For there are also some among those who appear to be in communion with him and with his synod who blaspheme the Holy Spirit, speaking rightly about the Son but holding the Spirit to be created and wholly alien to God; about these we shall later, in the refutation of their heresy, say everything precisely, as far as we are able.

**73,35,1a** The man, then, is held in honour by us, as I said, because of such reports about him.

**73,35,1b** For in other respects too his life is dignified and his character good, and he is beloved by the people in every way, since his life is extolled as godlike by all.

**73,35,2** But some — whether carried away by hatred or by envy, or wishing to magnify their own cause, I cannot say — have put about certain accounts concerning him too, to the effect that the movement against him came about not because of orthodoxy, but, they say, because of canonical matters and a squabble between him and his own clergy, and because he had admitted some whom he had long before expelled and anathematised.

**73,35,3a** But we have not at all taken these things to heart, chiefly because of what was afterwards corrected day by day in his synod and confessed in the faith, as I have already shown above.

**73,35,3b** For in this part one must speak the truth as far as one can, according to our weakness in all things.

**73,35,4a** For whether it escaped the man in the rush of his exposition of the words, I cannot say; whether the expression was brought out by him in simplicity, is known to God.

**73,35,4b** Except that in one part two or three blameworthy expressions are found in the same exposition: in his taking up the term ‘creature’ at all concerning the Son of God in his Godhead, even if only as far as the name, and in his saying ‘beyond wisdom’, and whatever else there may be.

**73,36,1a** After saying a few things in answer to what they have put forward, we shall pass over this account too.

**73,36,1b** Tell us, you people: what pained you about calling the ‘homoiousios’ ‘homoousios’?

**73,36,1c** Confess it to us plainly, so that we may recognise you too as our own and not as strangers.

**73,36,1d** For bronze too can be ‘homoiousios’ with gold, tin with silver, lead with iron.

**73,36,1e** But your contrived and finely turned myth-making will not deceive us.

**73,36,2** For if, wishing to deceive some, you choose to put forward false pretexts, saying that one must not say ‘homoousios’, lest we make a fusion of the Son with the Father, or of the Spirit with Son and Father, then in this too your contrived argument has fallen to pieces.

**73,36,3** For we did not say ‘hamaousios’ but ‘homoousios’, so that we might confess nothing differing from the Father, but God truly begotten of God, and not from elsewhere, nor from things that are not, but come forth from the Father, begotten timelessly, without beginning and indescribably, ever being with the Father and never ceasing to be, but begotten — not a brother, not a forefather.

**73,36,4a** For ‘homou’ signifies two hypostases that are not alien in nature; therefore the bond of truth in this word was arranged by the Holy Spirit in the mouth of those who set it forth, and you observe that no pretext will be left to you, nor can you speak against orthodoxy and frighten those who accept from you what they hear of your counterfeit doctrine, saying that if anyone says ‘homoousios’ he has confessed a fusion.

**73,36,4b** For this will no longer hold.

**73,36,5** For from ‘homoousios’ two will be signified, and from ‘homoousios’ it will be made plain that the offspring is not alien to the Father.

**73,36,6** But you, who have fabricated ‘homoiousios’, will be convicted by the term ‘essence’, and condemned by your altered confession, as not thinking what you say, but teaching in counterfeit form what you think; for if he is not from him at all, but is like him, you have strayed far from the truth.

**73,36,7a** For with whatever materials anyone might wish to adorn the one being portrayed, he would not produce something equal to the one portrayed; for the work, too, is a matter of craftsmanship.

**73,36,7b** But what is begotten of someone preserves, in relation to its kind, the like and equal form of legitimate birth.

**73,36,8** If, then, the Son has not been begotten of the Father himself, but should be outside him, and is to be called ‘homoiousios’ by you by grace, you have given him nothing, but have fallen from the grace that comes from him.

**73,36,9a** “For he who does not honour the Son as he honours the Father, the wrath of God abides on him,” says the holy apostle.

**73,36,9b** And again: “From the Father I came forth, and I am come.”

**73,36,9c** He who declared, “I am within the Father, and the Father within me”; he who says, “Philip, he who has seen me has seen the Father.”

**73,37,1** Having often given an account of these matters too, we think we are sufficiently provided here with the same refutations that were given above against the root which put forth these people’s wrong belief, since they are able here too to refute these Semi-Arians already mentioned, and those who split off from them,

**73,37,2** Acacius and his party and the others who set forth at Seleucia in Isauria another creed contrary to that of the truth; and this creed too, set forth by them and written in the name of them all, we have placed above in its entirety, likewise after Basil of Ancyra’s and George of Laodicea’s, wishing to bring it into the open.

**73,37,3** But so that I may not seem to have done this through forgetfulness, by treating as secondary this creed too, which works its mischief in secret but has taken a muzzle upon its mouth, as with a bridle, because of the season of hypocrisy, I shall also say a few things against it and against those who set it forth, the aforementioned party of Acacius, Euzoius, Eutychius and the others.

**73,37,4a** Now it is evident that the creed set out above has changed the confession of the truth.

**73,37,4b** But so that some may not say that we have spoken against these men by way of slander, let us show what, as time went on, was seen and detected in the aforementioned synod of these same men;

**73,37,5a** for from among them is Euzoius of Caesarea, being their disciple, even though he succeeded Acacius after the installation of Philumenus, who was installed by Cyril of Jerusalem, and after the installation of Cyril the elder, who was installed by Eutychius’ party, and after the installation of Gelasius, who was installed in turn by Cyril of Jerusalem; for he was his sister’s son.

**73,37,5b** For when the three had been installed and had been left idle because of their strife with one another, the aforementioned Euzoius was installed in turn.

**73,37,6a** From among them, then, was Gemellinus as well; from among them Philip of Scythopolis; from among them Athanasius of Scythopolis.

**73,37,6b** These men, not in secret but openly, as men without experience of the good, not only teach the doctrines of Arius but fight hard for their heresy, and persecute those who teach the truth, no longer wishing to refute them with words, but handing over those who believe rightly to hostilities, wars and swords.

**73,37,6c** For they have wrought ruin not on one city and country, but on many.

**73,38,1a** This is the Lucius who did so many things in Alexandria against those who confess the Son of God in truth.

**73,38,1b** And to which of those who have understanding of God is their faction not evident day by day?

**73,38,1c** For they proclaim publicly that the Son of God is created, and that the Holy Spirit too is created and wholly alien to the essence of God.

**73,38,2a** For as to Eudoxius and his party: ever since George of Alexandria shamefully met his end, he also received the first place, and friendship with the authority that is pre-eminent.

**73,38,2b** Eudoxius, who was of the party of Hypatius and Eunomius, appeared through a kind of flattery as one under reproof, yet did not cease to hold the views of the Anomoeans,

**73,38,3** while concealing those whom they had once exiled for such an exposition of the pit; he himself advanced Demophilus, Hypatius and Eunomius, the pupils of Aetius — the man once banished to the regions of the Taurus, whom George of Alexandria had installed as deacon — from whom the root of the Anomoeans sprang;

**73,38,4** and just as, though the thorny wood is one and the root the same, the branchings differ as on each thorn, so too the malice of these people, with the misinterpretations of their heterodox sect advancing for the worse, in one way at one time and in another way at another, has spewed out its ruin upon the world, as we shall again say later concerning this Anomoean.

**73,38,5** For the present, thinking it well to stop here, and having, as it were, overturned and thrust aside a dreadful reptile — we have indeed overturned it — let us trample it and leave it dead, and, turning aside, hasten on to those that follow, calling on God to help us likewise to fulfil our promise.

### Sect 74: Pneumatomachi

Against the Pneumatomachi, the fifty-fourth, but the seventy-fourth in the series.

**74,1,1** From these Semi-Arians and from some of the orthodox, men have risen up against us, born to some, so to speak, as a monstrosity, double-natured and half-formed, like the Centaurs, or Pans, or Sirens of those who wrote down the myths:

**74,1,2** some of them, being from Arius and professing to define the Son not as a perfect creature but as a Son timelessly begotten — though they speak of him who is from heaven and hither with a suggestion of time, not being freed from the expression first spewed out by Arius, which says that there was once when he was not — saying that he is before all times, he through whom all things came into being, blaspheme the Holy Spirit.

**74,1,3a** Others hold orthodox views concerning the Son also as to nature: that he always was with the Father and never ceased to be.

**74,1,3b** But though they hold that he was begotten of the Father without beginning and timelessly, against the Holy Spirit all these blaspheme, since they do not count him together with Father and Son within the Godhead.

**74,1,4a** We have often discussed this at length, and in each heresy we have set out in no small measure the true account concerning him, how he is properly spoken of together with the Father and the Son.

**74,1,4b** For “the Spirit of the Lord has filled the inhabited earth”: the Spirit of the truth, the Spirit of God.

**74,1,4c** For he is named Spirit of the Lord, both as going forth from the Father and as taking from the Son, bestowing the gifts in various ways as he wills, searching even the depths of God, being with the Father and the Son, baptising, sealing, perfecting the one who has been sealed.

**74,1,5a** But so as not to take on labour here, I shall set down what I have already said in the great treatise on the faith written to the regions of the Pamphylians, as a rebuttal of those who blaspheme the Holy Spirit, for the instruction of those who read it, and for the delight of those counted worthy of the Holy Spirit.

**74,1,5b** And it is as follows.

**74,1,5c** Discourse from the Ancoratus.

**74,2,1** “The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ has been made manifest, instructing us that, renouncing ungodliness and the desires of the world, we should live with self-control, with piety and with uprightness in this present age, awaiting the blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of our great God and Saviour Jesus Christ; who gave himself on our behalf, to ransom us from every lawless deed and to cleanse for himself a people peculiarly his own, eager for good works;

**74,2,2** having wiped out the bond written against us in its decrees, which stood opposed to us, he has removed it from our midst, nailing it to the cross; having stripped the principalities and the authorities, he exposed them publicly, leading them in triumph in it; having smashed the doors of bronze and crushed the bars of iron”, he showed once more the light of life, holding out his hands, making a road, pointing out the stairway to the heavens, deeming us worthy to dwell once again in paradise.

**74,2,3** Accordingly he dwelt among us, and, giving us the just requirement of the law of the Spirit, so that we might know him or the things concerning him — which is the beginning and end of life — he has become for us a law of righteousness, a law of faith, a law of the Spirit, set free of the law of the flesh of sin.

**74,2,4a** Hence “I rejoice in God’s law according to the inward man.”

**74,2,4b** And let Christ be ours, if indeed he dwells in us.

**74,2,5a** But he himself, by dying, has become a way of life for us, “that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for him who died for us and rose again”, the cause of life, having remembered the oath sworn many generations before, as David says.

**74,2,5b** “God was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself, not reckoning their trespasses to them.

**74,2,6** For in him the whole fullness was pleased to make its dwelling, and through him to reconcile all things to him, making peace by the blood of the cross.”

**74,2,7** He has come, therefore, for a dispensation of the fullness of the seasons, just as had been promised to Abraham and to the rest of the saints, to gather up all things under one head in himself, both what is in the heavens and what is upon the earth.

**74,2,8a** There was estrangement and enmity in the time of God’s forbearance, but he brought reconciliation in his body of flesh, through himself making the two into one.

**74,2,8b** “For our peace came, and, having broken down the middle wall of the partition, the enmity, in his flesh, having abolished the law of commandments in ordinances, that he might create the two in himself into one new man.”

**74,2,8c** And he commanded that the Gentiles be fellow members of the body, sharers and joint heirs of the promise, saying, “Come to me, all who toil and are weighed down with burdens, and I will refresh you.”

**74,2,9** Accordingly, in that I was weak through the flesh, the Saviour was sent to me in a likeness of the flesh of sin, fulfilling such a dispensation, that he might redeem me from slavery, that he might redeem me from corruption, that he might redeem me from death.

**74,2,10a** And he became for me righteousness and sanctification and redemption: righteousness, by having loosed sin through faith in him; sanctification, by having freed me by means of water and Spirit and in his word; and redemption, his blood.

**74,2,10b** He gave himself up for me as the ransom of a true lamb, a propitiation for the cleansing of the world, for the reconciliation of all things in heaven and on earth, fulfilling at the times appointed the mystery that was concealed from before the ages and the generations.

**74,2,11** The same “will refashion the body of our lowliness so that it becomes conformed to his glory, by the working of his power even to subject all things to himself”, because “in him all the fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily.”

**74,3,1a** Christ, then, is the receptacle of wisdom and Godhead, mediating and reconciling all things to God in himself, not reckoning sin, fulfilling hidden mysteries by faith in his covenant promised beforehand by the law and the prophets, proclaimed Son of God, called Son of David.

**74,3,1b** For he is both God and man, mediator of God and men, God’s true house, a holy priesthood, giver of the Spirit who regenerates and renews all things again for God.

**74,3,1c** “And the Word became flesh and pitched his tent among us, and we saw his glory, glory as of an only-begotten from a Father.”

**74,3,2a** Rain, uniting in growth with trees and plants, forms a body, and in each the fruit after its likeness.

**74,3,2b** And in the olive it becomes rich oil, taking on its substance from it; in the vine it is coloured as sweet wine; in the fig tree it is sweetened into a fig; and in each of the seeds it increases the growth according to its kind:

**74,3,3** so, I think, the Word of God came to be in Mary and was found a man in the seed of Abraham, according to the promise, “For we have found Messiah, whom Moses wrote of.”

**74,3,4a** And as Moses said, “Let my utterance come down as rain, and as drops falling upon the earth.

**74,3,4b** Or let it come down as dew upon a fleece.”

**74,3,4c** Wool, then, receiving the dew, increases the growth of the fleece, and earth, receiving the rain, the husbandman of hope, increases fruit by receiving it at the Master’s command, readily contributing its own nature.

**74,3,4d** But it is the more eager to receive from it.

**74,3,5a** So too the Virgin Mary: “By what shall I know this,” she says, “that it will be so for me?”

**74,3,5b** She heard, “The Spirit of the Lord upon you, and the power of the Most High, shall overshadow you.

**74,3,5c** Therefore also that which is born of you shall be holy and shall be called Son of the Most High.”

**74,3,6a** Christ speaks in the angel, and the Master refashions himself in his own handiwork, taking the form of a servant.

**74,3,6b** And Mary draws up the Word for conception, as the earth the rain, while the Word of God shows himself a holy fruit, taking on the nature of a mortal.

**74,3,7a** He it was, from her who drew him up as earth and fleeces do, the fruit of the true hope, looked for by the saints, even as Elizabeth was saying, “Blessed you are among women, and blessed the fruit of your womb.”

**74,3,7b** In what he took from humanity the Word suffered, though he is impassible.

**74,3,8a** “This is the living bread, the one who came down out of heaven”, and who gives life; this is the fruit of the true olive tree, the oil of the anointing and of the compounding, whom Moses prefigured.

**74,3,8b** He is the true vine, which the Father alone tends,

**74,3,9a** having brought forth for us a cluster of joy; he is “the living water, which a thirsty man receives and will thirst no more, but it is in his belly, welling up to life eternal.”

**74,3,9b** Receiving from him, the new husbandmen shared it with the world, but the old husbandmen dried it up and ruined it through unbelief.

**74,3,10a** With his own blood he sanctifies the nations, and by the eternal Spirit he leads the called into the heavens.

**74,3,10b** As many, then, as are led by his Spirit, these live to God; but as many as are not are still reckoned to death, and these are called natural, that is, fleshly.

**74,3,11** Accordingly he sets aside the works of the flesh, since it is a stronghold of sin, and puts to death the members of death through his grace, and the Holy Spirit, which we did not possess, he bids us receive, which gives life to me who had long been dead, and without receiving which I shall die; for without his Spirit everyone is dead.

**74,3,12a** “If, then, his Spirit is in us, he who raised him from the dead will give life to our mortal bodies through his Spirit that dwells in us.”

**74,3,12b** But, I think, both dwell in the righteous man, Christ and his Spirit.

**74,4,1a** But if Christ is believed to be from the Father, God from God, and his Spirit from Christ, or from both — as Christ says, “which goes forth from the Father”, and “this one will take from what is mine” — and Christ is of the Holy Spirit.

**74,4,1b** For “that which is in her,” it says, “is of the Holy Spirit” — the voice of an angel.

**74,4,1c** I grasp the mystery which ransoms me through faith, through hearing only, through affection for the one who has come to me.

**74,4,2a** For it is God who knows himself; Christ preaches himself; and the Holy Spirit makes himself plain to those who are worthy.

**74,4,2b** In the holy Scriptures a Trinity is proclaimed to us and believed, without curious inquiry and without contention, through the hearing of its watchwords.

**74,4,2c** From faith in it comes the salvation of grace; it is written that righteousness is from faith apart from works of law,

**74,4,3** and that from the hearing of faith Christ’s Spirit is granted to those who are being saved.

**74,4,4a** And the catholic faith is signified by the voices of heralds thus, as I at least think, having been instructed from the Scriptures: three holy, three co-holy; three existent, three co-existent; three in form, three conformed; three active, three co-operating; three subsistent, three co-subsistent, being together with one another; this is called a holy Trinity: being three, one harmony, one Godhead of the same power, of the same hypostasis, like from like, it works the equality of grace — of the same grace — of Father and Son and Holy Spirit.

**74,4,4b** But the how he has left to them to teach.

**74,4,5a** “No one knows the Father except the Son, nor the Son but the Father and anyone to whom the Son reveals.”

**74,4,5b** And he reveals through the Holy Spirit.

**74,4,6** These three, then, being either from him, or by him, or towards him, are understood worthily by each one as they reveal themselves — light, fire, spirit — and, I think, in other likenesses of activities, according as the man who is ministered to is worthy.

**74,4,7a** It is God himself, then, who in the beginning said, “Let there be light, and there was light”, the light that is seen; it is he himself who enlightened us to see “the true light, which enlightens every man coming into the world.”

**74,4,7b** “Send out your light and your truth,” says David.

**74,4,7c** He is the Lord who said, “In the last days I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh, and their daughters shall prophesy, and their young men shall see visions”, showing us three persons of holy ministry, since there is a third hypostasis from a hypostasis.

**74,4,7d** “I say, then, that Christ has become a servant of circumcision on behalf of God’s truth, so as to fulfil the promises”; and that the Holy Spirit ministers with him we have received from the divine Scriptures, as follows.

**74,4,7e** Christ is dispatched from the Father, and the Holy Spirit is dispatched; in the saints Christ speaks, and the Holy Spirit speaks; Christ gives healing, and the Holy Spirit gives healing.

**74,4,7f** Christ sanctifies, the Holy Spirit sanctifies.

**74,4,7g** Christ baptises in his name, the Holy Spirit baptises.

**74,4,7h** Thus the Scriptures say, “You will send forth your Spirit, and you will renew the face of the earth.”

**74,4,7i** This is like saying, “You will send out your word and melt them.”

**74,4,7j** “And as they were ministering to the Lord,” it says, “and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, Set apart now for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.”

**74,4,7k** This is like saying, “And the Lord says, Go into the city, and there you will be told what you must do.”

**74,4,7l** “So they, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia.”

**74,4,7m** As Christ might say, “Behold, I send you out as sheep in the midst of wolves.”

**74,4,7n** “For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit that no other burden be laid on you except the necessary things.”

**74,4,7o** As he might say, “But I say, not the Lord, that a wife is not to separate from her husband.”

**74,5,6a** “And they passed through Phrygia and the region of Galatia, having been forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia.

**74,5,6b** And when they had come to Mysia they tried to go into Bithynia, and the Holy Spirit did not allow them.”

**74,5,6c** As Christ might say, “Go and baptise among all the nations.”

**74,5,6d** “Carry no bag, no staff, nor sandals”; “who,” it says, “told Paul through the Spirit not to go up to Jerusalem.”

**74,5,7a** Or Agabus: “Thus says the Holy Spirit, The man whose belt this is.”

**74,5,7b** This is like what Paul said, “If you are looking for proof of the Christ who speaks within me”, or, “Keep in mind the Lord’s words, how he himself said, It is good to give rather than to receive.”

**74,5,8a** “And now, see, I am on my way, bound by the Spirit.”

**74,5,8b** As he might say, “Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ.”

**74,5,9a** “Except that the Spirit testifies to me in every city, saying.”

**74,5,9b** This is like what he said, “The Lord bears witness to my soul that I do not lie.”

**74,5,10a** “In power according to the Spirit of holiness.”

**74,5,10b** This is like saying, “Holy is he who rests among the holy.”

**74,5,11** And “circumcision of the heart in the Spirit” is like saying, “And he was circumcised with a circumcision not made by hand, in the stripping away of the body of sins, in the circumcision of Christ.”

**74,5,12a** “If indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you.”

**74,5,12b** This is like saying, “As you received Christ, walk in him.”

**74,5,12c** And, “The Lord’s Spirit spoke in me, and his word was in my mouth.”

**74,5,12d** And, “having the first fruits of the Spirit.”

**74,5,13** This is like saying, “Christ the first fruits.”

**74,5,14a** “But the Spirit himself intercedes for us.”

**74,5,14b** This is like saying, “who is at the right hand of God, who intercedes for us.”

**74,5,15a** “That the offering of the Gentiles may be acceptable, sanctified in the Holy Spirit.”

**74,5,15b** This is like saying, “And may the Lord sanctify you, that you may be pure and without offence for the day of the Lord.”

**74,5,16a** “But God has revealed it to us through his Spirit.”

**74,5,16b** This is like saying, “When he who had set me apart from my mother’s womb was well pleased, through his grace, to unveil his Son within me.”

**74,5,17a** “But it is not the world’s spirit that we received, but the Spirit of God.”

**74,5,17b** This is like saying, “Examine yourselves, whether Christ is in you.”

**74,5,18a** “A temple of God you are, and God’s Spirit dwells within you.”

**74,5,18b** This is like saying, “I shall make my dwelling in them and move about among them, and I shall be God to them, and they will be a people to me.”

**74,6,1a** But it also speaks of justification and of grace as coming from both.

**74,6,1b** “But having been justified in the name of Jesus Christ our Lord and in the Spirit of our God.”

**74,6,1c** This is like saying, “But having been justified out of faith, we have peace towards God through our Lord Jesus Christ.”

**74,6,2a** “No one is able to say ‘Lord Jesus’ except in the Holy Spirit”, and no one is able to receive Holy Spirit except from the Lord.

**74,6,2b** “There are distributions of gifts, but the Spirit is the same; and there are distributions of ministries, but the same God who works all things in all.”

**74,6,2c** And, “from glory to glory, as from the Lord the Spirit.”

**74,6,3a** And, “Do not grieve the Holy Spirit, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.”

**74,6,3b** This is like saying, “If we rouse the Lord’s jealousy, we are not stronger than he, are we?”

**74,6,4a** “But the Spirit says expressly.”

**74,6,4b** This is like saying, “Thus says the Lord Almighty.”

**74,6,5a** And, “My Spirit stands in your midst.”

**74,6,5b** “If anyone opens to me, I will come in, I and the Father, and we will make our abode with him.”

**74,6,6a** And Isaiah: “And upon him the Spirit of God.”

**74,6,6b** And Christ: “The Lord’s Spirit is on me, for the sake of which he has anointed me.”

**74,6,6c** And, “Jesus, the one from Nazareth, whom God anointed with Holy Spirit.”

**74,6,6d** Or, “The Lord has sent me, and his Spirit.”

**74,6,7** And plain too is the voice of the Seraphim, crying, “Holy, holy, holy, Lord of Sabaoth.”

**74,6,8a** And if you hear, “Exalted to the right hand of God, and having received the promise of the Spirit from the Father”, or, “to await the Father’s promise, which you heard.”

**74,6,8b** Or that the Spirit drives him out into the wilderness, or that he himself says, “Do not be anxious what you are to say, for it is the Spirit who speaks in you.”

**74,6,8c** Or, “But if I cast out the demons by the Spirit of God.”

**74,6,8d** Or, “But he who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit — for him there will be no forgiveness”, and what follows.

**74,6,8e** Or, “Father, into your hands I will commit my spirit.”

**74,6,8f** Or, “The child grew and became strong in the Spirit.”

**74,6,8g** Or, “And Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan.”

**74,6,8h** Or, “Jesus returned by the power of the Spirit.”

**74,6,8i** Or, “What has been born of the Spirit is spirit.”

**74,6,8j** This is like saying, “What came into being in him was life.”

**74,6,8k** Or, “And I will entreat the Father, and another Paraclete he will give you, the Spirit of truth.”

**74,6,8l** Or, “Why has Satan filled your heart,” he says to Ananias, “that you should lie to the Holy Spirit?”

**74,6,8m** And after this, “You have not lied to men but to God.”

**74,6,8n** So, then, the Holy Spirit is God from God, and God, the one to whom those who kept back part of the price of the field lied.

**74,6,8o** Or, “who was manifested in the flesh, justified in the Spirit.”

**74,6,8p** I can say nothing greater than this.

**74,6,9a** And the Son is God: “of whom,” it says, “is Christ according to the flesh, who is God over all.”

**74,6,9b** “Believe,” it says, “in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved.”

**74,6,9c** And, “He spoke the word of the Lord to them,” it says, “and he brought them up into his house and set a table before them, and rejoiced with all his household, having believed in God.”

**74,6,9d** Or, that “in the beginning the Word was, and the Word was in God’s presence, and the Word was God.”

**74,6,9e** Or, “that they may adorn the teaching of our Saviour.”

**74,6,9f** Or, “For the grace of our Lord and Saviour Christ has appeared to all men, teaching us.”

**74,6,9g** Or, “receiving the blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of our great God and Saviour Jesus Christ.”

**74,6,10a** Or: the ministry of the Spirit and of the Word is the same.

**74,6,10b** “Take heed,” it says, “to yourselves and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has made you bishops, to shepherd the church of God.”

**74,6,10c** This is like saying, “I give thanks to him who strengthens me, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he counted me faithful, appointing me to the ministry.”

**74,7,1a** The Son and the Holy Spirit, then, as has been demonstrated, work together with the Father.

**74,7,1b** For “by the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and by the Spirit of his mouth all his power.”

**74,7,1c** And the Holy Spirit is to be worshipped; for “those who worship God must worship in Spirit and in truth.”

**74,7,2a** And if the Truth works together with him, a creature does not make a creature, nor does the Godhead come to be created, nor is God known in measure or circumscription.

**74,7,2b** For he is uncircumscribed, uncontainable, inconceivable, encompassing all the works of God.

**74,7,3a** But the creation is not to be served in worship.

**74,7,3b** “For they served the creation rather than the Creator, and became fools.”

**74,7,3c** For how is it not foolish to call a creature God, and to set aside the Father’s command that says, “Listen, Israel: the Lord your God is one; there shall be no new god among you”?

**74,7,4** In the holy Scriptures various names are used for Father, Son and Holy Spirit: for the Father, almighty Father, Father of all things, Christ’s Father; for the Lord, Word, Christ, Son, true light; for the Holy Spirit, Paraclete, Spirit of truth, God’s Spirit, Christ’s Spirit.

**74,7,5a** Further, then, God and Father is conceived of as light — but as surpassingly bright — as power, as wisdom.

**74,7,5b** And if the God and Father is light, light from light is the Son, and for this reason he dwells in light unapproachable.

**74,7,6a** And God is wholly power, and for this reason the Lord of powers.

**74,7,6b** God is wholly wisdom; therefore the Son is wisdom from wisdom, “in whom all the treasures of wisdom are hidden.”

**74,7,6c** And God is wholly life; therefore the Son is life from life.

**74,7,6d** “For it is I who am the truth and the life.”

**74,7,7a** And the Holy Spirit is from both, spirit from spirit.

**74,7,7b** For “God is spirit”; he is Godhead, the giver of gifts, most true, enlightening, consoling, the herald of the Father’s counsels.

**74,7,8a** For as the Son is the angel of great counsel, so also is the Holy Spirit.

**74,7,8b** “But we received,” it says, “the Spirit of God, so that we may see the things graciously given us by God, which we also speak, not with persuasive words of wisdom but with a showing of God’s Spirit, matching spiritual things with spiritual.”

**74,8,1a** But someone will say: Then do we say that there are two sons, and how is he only-begotten?

**74,8,1b** Nay rather, “Who are you who argue against God?”

**74,8,1c** For if he calls Son the one who is from him, and Holy Spirit the one who is from both — who are conceived by the saints by faith alone, luminous and light-giving — they have a luminous operation, and by faith in the light they form a harmony with the Father himself.

**74,8,2** Hear, you there, that the Father is truly Father of a Son, wholly light, and the Son is Son of a true Father, light from light, not by appellation only, as things made or created are; and the Holy Spirit is Spirit of truth, a light that is third, from Father and Son; but all other things are so by adoption,

**74,8,3a** or by juxtaposition, or by calling, not by an operation, or power, or light, or conception like his: or as someone might put it, “I have begotten and exalted sons.”

**74,8,3b** Or as one might say, “I said, You are gods, and all of you sons of the Most High.”

**74,8,3c** Or as one might say, “he who has begotten the drops of dew.”

**74,8,3d** Or as one might say, “from whom every fatherhood in heaven and on earth.”

**74,8,3e** Or as one might say, “I am he who makes firm the thunder and creates spirit.”

**74,8,4a** For the true Father did not, like the other fathers or patriarchs, begin to be father, nor is he ever, at any time, wanting in being father.

**74,8,4b** For if he begins to be father, then he was once the son of another father, before he was father of the Only-begotten.

**74,8,4c** By likeness, fathers are understood to be children of fathers, and the one who is truly father of the ancient line is to be found only by going back to infinity.

**74,8,5a** Nor is the true Son, like the other children by adoption, new in being son.

**74,8,5b** For if he is new in being son, there was once a time when the Father was not Father of an only-begotten.

**74,8,6a** Nor is the Spirit of truth created or made, like the other spirits.

**74,8,6b** Nor is the angel of great counsel called so in the way the other angels are.

**74,8,7a** For some have beginning and end, while others have a might and an origin beyond conception; and some create all things for endless ages, working together with the Father, while others are created by them as they may will.

**74,8,7b** And some serve these, while others are served in worship by all creatures; and some heal the things made, while others receive healing from them.

**74,8,8a** And some are judged according to desert, while others hold the just judgement.

**74,8,8b** And some exist in time, while others are not in time.

**74,8,8c** And some enlighten all things, while others are enlightened.

**74,8,8d** And some bestow on all, while others receive gifts.

**74,8,8e** And, to put it once for all, some sing the praises of the holiness in the heavens of the heavens and the rest of the unseen places, while others, being hymned, worthily grant the gifts to the worthy.

**74,9,1a** Scripture speaks of very many spirits: “he who makes his angels into spirits, and his ministers into a flame of fire.”

**74,9,1b** And, “All you spirits, praise the Lord.”

**74,9,2a** And gifts of discernment of spirits are given to the worthy.

**74,9,2b** For some are heavenly, rejoicing in the truth; some earthly, apt for deceit and error; and some beneath the earth, children of the abyss and of darkness.

**74,9,2c** “For he begged him,” the gospel says, “not to send him away into the abyss.”

**74,9,2d** Likewise he gave commands to the spirits.

**74,9,2e** And he drove out spirits with a word and did not allow them to speak.

**74,9,3a** There is spoken of also a spirit of judgement and a spirit of burning.

**74,9,3b** And there is spoken of a spirit of the world.

**74,9,3c** “But the spirit of the world is not what we received,” it says; and the spirit of a man as well: “For who knows the things of a man except the spirit that is in the man?”

**74,9,3d** And, “a spirit that goes forth and does not return; for a spirit passed through it, and it shall be no more.”

**74,9,3e** And, “You will take away their spirit, and they will fail.”

**74,9,4a** And, “The spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.”

**74,9,4b** And, “See, a spirit of falsehood stood in the Lord’s presence, and he said to it, By what means will you deceive Ahab?

**74,9,4c** And I shall be,” it says, “a spirit of falsehood in the prophets’ mouth.”

**74,9,5a** There is said to be also a spirit of stupor, a spirit of cowardice, and a spirit of Python and a spirit of fornication and a spirit of tempest and a spirit of many words and a spirit of infirmity and an unclean spirit and a deaf spirit and a dumb spirit and a stammering spirit and an exceedingly fierce spirit, which is called Legion, and the spiritual hosts of wickedness.

**74,9,5b** Countless, for the wise, are the sayings about spirits.

**74,9,6a** But just as the many sons are sons by adoption or by calling, and not in truth, because they have a beginning and an end and are liable to sin, so too the very many spirits are spirits by adoption or by calling, even if they were sinful.

**74,9,6b** But the Holy Spirit alone is called by the Father and the Son the Spirit of truth and Spirit of God and Spirit of Christ and Spirit of grace.

**74,9,7** For he bestows the good on each in various ways: on one a spirit of wisdom, on another a spirit of knowledge, on another a spirit of strength, on another a spirit of healings, on another a spirit of prophecy, on another a spirit of discernment, on another interpretations, and the other gifts as well, as it says, “But one and the same Spirit, distributing to each as he wills.”

**74,9,8a** Or, “Your good Spirit shall lead me, O God,” says David.

**74,9,8b** Or, “The Spirit blows where he wills” — by these words he shows us the real subsistence of the Holy Spirit — “and you hear his voice, but you do not know where he comes from and where he goes”, and, “unless you are born of water and Spirit.”

**74,9,8c** This is like what Paul said, “For it was I who begot you in Christ Jesus.”

**74,9,9a** Of him the Lord says, “When the Paraclete comes, whom I send to you, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, he will bear witness concerning me.”

**74,9,9b** And, “Still I have many things to say, but you cannot carry them at present.

**74,9,9c** When he comes, the Spirit of truth will guide you into all the truth.

**74,9,9d** For he will not speak of himself, but whatever he hears he will speak, and he will declare to you the things to come.

**74,9,9e** He will glorify me, for he will receive of mine and will declare all things to you.”

**74,10,1** If, then, he proceeds from the Father, and “he will receive of mine,” says the Lord.

**74,10,2** In the way that no one knew the Father except the Son, nor the Son except the Father, so, I venture to say, no one knows the Spirit either, save the Son, from whom he takes, and the Father, out of whom he goes forth; nor the Son and the Father, save the Holy Spirit, who glorifies truly, who teaches all things, who bears witness to the things concerning the Son, who is from the Father, who is of the Son, the sole guide to truth, interpreter of holy laws, the one who expounds the spiritual law, teacher of the prophets, master of the apostles, luminary of the doctrines of the gospel, chooser of the saints; the true light from true light,

**74,10,3** Son by nature, true Son, true-born Son, only from only; with him also the Spirit, but named Spirit.

**74,10,4a** This is God, glorified in the church.

**74,10,4b** Father always, Son always, and Holy Spirit always; high from the high, and most high, having an intellectual glory beyond measure, to whom created and made things are subject — in a word, all things together, each of them measured and contained.

**74,10,5a** One Godhead is proclaimed above all in Moses, the Dyad is strongly preached in the prophets, and the Trinity is made manifest in the gospels, suiting the righteous more fully, according to times and generations, for knowledge and faith.

**74,10,5b** And this knowledge is of immortality, and from faith in it comes adoption.

**74,10,6a** But first it sets forth ordinances of the flesh, as if raising up the outer enclosure of the temple, in Moses.

**74,10,6b** Second, it recounts ordinances of the soul, as if adorning the holy place, in the rest of the prophecies; third, ordinances of the spirit, as if setting in order the mercy seat and the holy of holies, in the gospels, for its own indwelling.

**74,10,6c** And as its holy tabernacle and holy people it has only the righteous man, who abides with these.

**74,10,7** And in him dwells one incorruptible Godhead, one Godhead inconceivable, incomprehensible, indescribable, invisible, alone knowing itself, manifesting itself to whom it wills, raising up witnesses for itself, calling, foreordaining, glorifying, raising up from Hades, sanctifying,

**74,10,8** uniting again to its own glory and faith these threes: things heavenly and earthly and under the earth; spirit, soul, flesh; faith, hope, love; things past, present, to come; the age of the age, ages of ages, sabbaths of sabbaths; circumcision of the flesh, circumcision of the heart, the circumcision of Christ in the putting off of the body of sins.

**74,10,9a** In sum, it makes pure for itself all things invisible and visible, thrones, dominions, principalities, authorities, powers.

**74,10,9b** And in all is the same wisdom and holy voice, from glory to glory, crying “Holy, holy, holy”: Father in Son, and Son in Father together with the Holy Spirit, to whom belong the glory and the might for the ages of ages.

**74,10,9c** Amen.

**74,10,9d** And whoever believes in this way will say, “Let it be so, let it be so.”

**74,10,9e** The extract from the Ancoratus is concluded.

**74,11,1a** These, then, are the things which, in writing about the faith in Father, Son and Holy Spirit, we have already expounded within the very narrow compass of our modest ability, and have set down from what was said before.

**74,11,1b** But we shall continue further, for the establishing of our own life, piously bringing forward testimonies and piously treating of the Godhead from right reasoning.

**74,11,2a** For that, in what precedes, the Only-begotten was shown through many testimonies to act together with the Father, accomplishing and bestowing equal things in all respects, as being from him, and not different from the power and Godhead of the Father, but consubstantial with the Father — and not the Son alone, but the Holy Spirit too, acting together with the Son and the Father, working equal things, giving and bestowing as he wills, as being himself truly from God, and not alien to Father and Son but consubstantial with Father and Son — this has been demonstrated, and will be demonstrated, as plain to everyone in every respect from so many testimonies.

**74,11,2b** But now, because of the adversaries and enemies of the Holy Spirit, after setting out, concerning the Holy Spirit alone, the pious conclusions of right reasoning and those drawn from testimonies of the same divine Scripture, we shall add more abundantly to the earlier testimonies, in keeping with true piety concerning the Holy Spirit.

**74,11,4** For as he is and exists, the Holy Spirit is indwelling, worshipped by all, longed for by all things created and made, made equal to none, not to an angel, not to another spirit, but unique.

**74,11,5a** For since there are indeed many spirits, but this one is the highest of all spirits, as being always from the Father and not from the others that came into being from things that are not.

**74,11,5b** For there are many spirits, but one Holy Spirit, even as God is one and God’s only-begotten Son is one.

**74,11,5c** So too is the Holy Spirit of God, from God and in God.

**74,11,6a** Now the only-begotten Son is beyond comprehension, and the Spirit is beyond comprehension, yet from God, and not alien to Father and Son.

**74,11,6b** Yet he is not in fusion with Father and Son, but it is a Trinity ever being of the same essence, not of another essence besides the Godhead, nor another Godhead besides the essence, but Godhead itself, and the Son and the Holy Spirit are of the same Godhead.

**74,11,7a** And the Spirit is Holy Spirit, and the Son is Son.

**74,11,7b** And the Spirit goes forth from the Father and takes from the Son, searching the depths of God, declaring the things of the Son in the world, sanctifying, making saints through the Trinity; third in naming, since the Trinity is Father and Son and Holy Spirit.

**74,11,7c** For “go,” it says, “and baptise into the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit”: the seal of grace, the bond of the Trinity, not alien to the sanctification, not separate in the naming, not alien to the gift, but one God, one faith, one Lord, one grace, one church, one baptism.

**74,12,1a** For the Trinity is ever, as I have often said, and the Trinity never receives addition, as it is sweet to confess and to say without being sated.

**74,12,1b** “For sweet,” says the prophet, “are your words to my throat.”

**74,12,2a** And if the sayings are sweet, how much the more the holy name, the Trinity, the fount of all sweetness?

**74,12,2b** The Trinity, then, is numbered thus: Father and Son and Holy Spirit.

**74,12,3a** But the Trinity is not a fusion, nor is it separated from its own unity.

**74,12,3b** But in a hypostasis of perfection: perfect is the Father, perfect the Son, perfect the Holy Spirit — Father and Son and Holy Spirit.

**74,12,4** And in the gifts the Spirit is placed in the reverse order: for “there are distributions of gifts, while the Spirit is the same; and distributions of ministries there are, but the same Lord; and there are distributions of workings, but the same God, who works all things in all.”

**74,12,5a** This being so, let us make ourselves secure, lest we fall from the truth; rather, let us confess the truth, not as advocates pleading on God’s behalf, but understanding piously, so that we may not perish.

**74,12,5b** For it is inadmissible to speak of, or to think of, anything created in the Trinity, or anything begotten later; but there always was Father and Son and Holy Spirit.

**74,12,6** The Son is neither a brother of the Father nor a fusion with him; and the Spirit is neither a fusion nor a brother to Father and Son, nor is the Spirit a fusion with Father and Son.

**74,12,7** But the Son is one begotten from the Father, and the Spirit one who came forth from the Father, indescribably, the Trinity being in an identity of glorification, and incomprehensibly, the Son being with the Father, and the Holy Spirit likewise, and the Trinity never falling short of the same everlastingness.

**74,12,8a** The Father, then, is ever unbegotten, not created, and beyond comprehension; the Son is begotten, yet not created and beyond comprehension.

**74,12,8b** The Holy Spirit is ever, not begotten, not created, not a brother, not a forefather, not a descendant, but of the same essence as Father and Son.

**74,12,8c** For “God is spirit.”

**74,13,1a** The testimonies to this life of ours, thus made secure, are found throughout all Scripture.

**74,13,1b** Out of the many I shall set down a few, as far as possible, so that in the present place too I may not pass over the account of the Spirit without testimony.

**74,13,2** For at once the Father says concerning the coming of the Son, “I shall set my Spirit on him, and he will announce judgement to the nations”, so that he might proclaim his Holy Spirit to be true God, to all the faithful, for salvation.

**74,13,3** And if the Only-begotten, adding to the same testimony, declares, “The Lord’s Spirit is on me, on account of which he has anointed me”, it is so that his coming in the flesh, made secure by the Holy Spirit too and proclaimed to the faithful, may be plainly confessed from Christ’s testimony, namely that the Spirit is not alien to God.

**74,13,4a** And again the Lord says of the Spirit that “it is the Spirit of my Father who speaks in you.”

**74,13,4b** And again, since the Spirit is not alien to the Godhead of God, he breathed into the face of the disciples and said, “Take the Holy Spirit.”

**74,13,4c** And again, to show his own equality and consubstantiality with the Holy Spirit, his own and his Father’s, he says, “If you love me, you will keep my commandments.

**74,13,4d** I shall ask the Father, and he shall grant you another Paraclete”, the Lord himself being a Paraclete, and the Holy Spirit likewise being a fellow Paraclete.

**74,13,5** And the apostles, showing that the Spirit is not a slave but of the same Godhead, and pointing to his authority, say, “And the Holy Spirit said, Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them”, and what follows.

**74,13,6a** And the apostle says plainly about them, “But the Lord is the Spirit, and wherever the Lord’s Spirit is, there is freedom.”

**74,13,6b** And, “You are God’s temple, and the Lord’s Spirit makes its dwelling in you.”

**74,13,7a** If, then, we are called God’s temple on account of the indwelling of the Holy Spirit, who could venture to disown the Spirit and make him a stranger to the essence of God, when the apostle states clearly that we become temples of God on account of the Holy Spirit dwelling within the worthy?

**74,13,7b** And how will the Spirit be alien to God, when he searches the depths of God?

**74,13,8** And do not tell me, “He searches, and does not yet know”, as some dare to blaspheme and to destroy themselves, since they would say the same of the Father too, for of him also it is written that “he searches the chambers of the belly.”

**74,13,9a** And if you think impiously, because ‘knowing’ is not attached to ‘searching’ in the case of the Spirit, you would commit impiety concerning the Father too, being forced to bring the same suspicion against him.

**74,13,9b** For neither in the case of the Father, who searches the chambers of the belly, is ‘knowing’ added, nor was there any need to say it, since the foreknowledge of God, which carries the completeness of the declaration, is plainly shown by the ‘searching’.

**74,13,9c** So too, to my mind, with regard to Spirit and Son and Father, the holy Trinity plainly has the one knowledge and the foreknowledge, both its perfection and its identity.

**74,14,1** And there are untold things one could say about these matters, and one could bring a mass of testimonies from divine Scripture, and draw the discussion out at length, and cause weariness to the readers.

**74,14,2** For having said a great deal, sufficiently, in every heresy, we, the weak, have by the power of God overthrown them all and shown them to be alien to the truth, each of them blaspheming and denying the truth, whether in a small matter or a great one; as these too blaspheme in vain against the Lord and against the Holy Spirit, and have no forgiveness of sins, neither here nor in the age to come, according to what the Lord said, because of the blasphemy against the Holy Spirit; they are trampled down by the truth itself,

**74,14,3** like a dread horned viper with a single horn — the mind of blasphemy, which can corrupt the whole body — being persuaded by the word of the Tree and by the true confession of the Only-begotten, that to him who blasphemes against the Spirit it shall not be forgiven, neither in this age nor in the age to come; trampled down, as I said, and crushed, having no strength against the truth.

**74,14,4** For all the heresies are truly gates of Hades, but they will not overpower the rock — the truth, that is; for even if some of them should choose to say, “We too confess the faith set out at Nicaea, but prove to me out of it that the Holy Spirit is counted in the Godhead”, they will be found to be refuted by it as well.

**74,14,5a** At that time the inquiry concerning the Spirit had not arisen.

**74,14,5b** For synods provide their safeguards against whatever arises at one time or another.

**74,14,5c** Since, then, Arius directed his slander against the Son, for this reason precision of language was achieved, with abundant discussion.

**74,14,6** But see from the confession itself that not even in this will those who blaspheme against the Spirit be found to have anything to say — the Pneumatomachi, strangers to his gift and his sanctification.

**74,14,7a** For the creed confesses at once, and does not deny.

**74,14,7b** For: “We believe in one God, Father almighty.”

**74,14,7c** And ‘we believe’ was not said idly, but the faith is towards God; and “in one Lord Jesus Christ.”

**74,14,7d** It was not said idly, but faith is directed to God; and “in the Holy Spirit” —

**74,14,8a** nor was this said idly, but unto one glorification and unto one union of Godhead and one consubstantiality: unto three perfect ones, but one Godhead, one essence, one glorification, one lordship, from ‘we believe’, and ‘we believe’, and ‘we believe’.

**74,14,8b** And here the argument of such people has collapsed.

**74,14,9a** And how far am I to lengthen the discussion, when I consider what has been said against these people sufficient for those who love the truth?

**74,14,9b** Therefore I shall pass over this one too, praying God to help us as usual towards the overthrow of all these, so that, having completed our undertaking in his power, we may give thanks to him in all things.

### Sect 75: Aerius

Against Aerius, the fifty-fifth, but the seventy-fifth in the series.

**75,1,1a** One Aerius has in turn likewise become a great evil to the world, thunderstruck in his understanding, puffed up in his mind.

**75,1,1b** For every heresy among those that have arisen, from the beginning to the end — it was the ill will of vainglory or of arrogance that wrought these things, or the craving of desire, or jealousy towards one’s neighbours, or provocation, or rashness.

**75,1,2** But the whole blinding is from the devil — not that the devil is able to deceive one who is unwilling, but each one becomes for himself the cause of his working at sin, “so that,” it says, “those who are approved may become manifest.”

**75,1,3a** This Aerius is still living in the flesh even now and survives in this life, an Arian through and through.

**75,1,3b** For he holds no other view but that of Arius, and goes still further beyond it, having sought out the doctrines of Arius, sharpened in tongue and armed in his lips in this respect, so as to draw to himself a deceived army and a multitude of those whose ears are ever being tickled and whose minds are slackened.

**75,1,4** For he too devised in his life a great and fabulous vainglory, which provokes laughter among sensible people; yet by it he deceived and drew away many.

**75,1,5a** This man was a fellow student of Eustathius of Sebaste — Sebaste, that is, in the region known as Pontus, or Lesser Armenia.

**75,1,5b** For the aforementioned Eustathius and Aerius practised the ascetic life together.

**75,1,6a** But when Eustathius came to the episcopate, Aerius desired it more, but did not attain to it.

**75,1,6b** From this arose jealousy.

**75,1,6c** Eustathius appeared to court Aerius assiduously.

**75,1,7a** Soon afterwards he makes him a presbyter and entrusts to him the hostel, which in Pontus is called a poorhouse.

**75,1,7b** For the heads of the churches construct such places out of hospitality, and, having the maimed and the infirm stay there, they provide for them as far as they are able.

**75,2,1a** Since, then, the resentment did not leave him, day by day the words grew and the jealousy between them advanced, and words that were not good, and slanders, were uttered by Aerius against Eustathius.

**75,2,1b** Bishop Eustathius summoned Aerius and flattered him, advised him, threatened him, rebuked him sternly, entreated him, and achieved nothing.

**75,2,1c** For what had been sown from the beginning was driving the business on to great evil.

**75,2,2** At last, then, Aerius left the poorhouse and withdrew; and from then on, like someone who wishes to find a pretext against an enemy, or to let fly a dart at a foe, he searched one out, and thereafter,

**75,2,3** slandering Eustathius to everyone, he said, “He is no longer what he was, but has turned to amassing money and to acquisitions of every kind.”

**75,2,4a** These things were slander on his part; in truth, Eustathius, having the needs of the church in his hands, could not act otherwise.

**75,2,4b** And what Aerius said was plausible.

**75,2,5a** Someone might suppose, since in speaking against Aerius we have brought Eustathius forward, that we perhaps hold Eustathius too in praise.

**75,2,5b** For not a few men admire his life and conduct —

**75,2,6a** and would that he had also thought rightly in the faith! For he too held to the doctrine of Arius from beginning to end, and not even the afflictions of the persecutions set him right.

**75,2,6b** For he was persecuted together with Basil, Eleusius and the rest.

**75,2,7** He also appeared to go as envoy, together with other bishops, to Liberius of Rome, of blessed memory, and to have subscribed to the creed of the council held at Nicaea and to the confession of orthodoxy.

**75,2,8a** But later, as though he had remembered and woken from dreams, he did not cease to return to his own former tenets of the Arian heterodoxy.

**75,2,8b** However, our discussion is about Aerius.

**75,2,8c** So we must return to him.

**75,3,1** This Aerius, because of such words, at first made a show of renunciation, and when he had left the poorhouse he drew away a great company of men and women.

**75,3,2a** And he himself, with his company, was driven away from the churches, and from the fields and villages and the other cities.

**75,3,2b** And often, with his own large crowd, they stayed out in the country, snowed upon, lodging in the open and under rocks, taking refuge in the woods.

**75,3,3a** His teaching was more maniacal than befits a sound human mind; and he says, “What does a bishop amount to beside a presbyter?”

**75,3,3b** “The one differs in nothing from the other; for there is one order and,” he says, “one honour and one dignity.”

**75,3,3c** “The bishop lays on hands,” he says, “but so does the presbyter.”

**75,3,3d** “The bishop administers the washing, and likewise the presbyter.”

**75,3,3e** “The bishop carries out the ordering of worship, and the presbyter in the same way.”

**75,3,3f** “The bishop sits on the throne; the presbyter sits on it too.”

**75,3,3g** By this he deceived many, and they have taken him as their leader.

**75,3,4a** Then he says, “What is the Passover that is celebrated among you?”

**75,3,4b** “You are again giving heed to Jewish fables.”

**75,3,4c** “For one ought not,” he says, “to celebrate the Passover.”

**75,3,4d** “For Christ, our Passover, was sacrificed.”

**75,3,5a** Then afterwards: “On what account,” he says, “do you name the names of the dead after death?”

**75,3,5b** “For the living man prays,” he says, “or has made some provision — what benefit will the dead man gain?”

**75,3,5c** “And if the prayer of those here has helped those there at all, then let no one live piously or do good, but let him acquire some friends by whatever means he likes, either persuading them with money or asking friends at his death, and let them pray on their behalf, so that he may suffer nothing there, and that the incurable sins he has committed may not be required of him.”

**75,3,6a** “Nor,” he says, “shall there be an appointed fast.”

**75,3,6b** “For these things are Jewish and under a yoke of slavery.”

**75,3,6c** “For law is not laid down for a just man, but for those who strike their fathers and those who strike their mothers, and the others.”

**75,3,6d** “For if I wish to fast at all, I fast of my own accord on whatever day I choose, because of my freedom.”

**75,3,6e** Hence among them it is rather made a point of pride to fast on the Lord’s day, and to eat on the fourth day and on the day before the sabbath.

**75,3,7** And often they do fast on the fourth day as well, not by rule but by their own choice, as he says.

**75,3,8** And in the days of the Passover, when among us there are sleeping on the ground, purifications, hardships, dry eating, prayers, vigils and fasts, and all the means of the souls’ salvation that belong to the holy passion, they from early morning buy in meat and wine, filling their veins, guffawing, laughing, mocking those who perform this sacred worship of Passover week.

**75,3,9a** For even though these people have adopted the manner of life of renunciants, ascetic practice is not carried on among them, but a great deal of meat-eating and wine-drinking — unless perhaps a rare few among them should wish this of their own choice.

**75,3,9b** Rather, the greater part of them indulge in abundant fare of flesh-eating and wine-drinking, as I have often said.

**75,3,9c** These are the things spewed out upon the world by Aerius.

**75,4,1** This, then, displays his notion and his unbelief, and the things that through him have in turn been thundered into the world as a craft of mischief.

**75,4,2a** But we shall come to the arguments against him, relating a few things and so passing on.

**75,4,2b** That the whole of it is full of folly is plain to those who possess understanding — his claim that bishop and presbyter are equal.

**75,4,2c** And how will this be possible?

**75,4,2d** For the one is an order that begets fathers, since it begets fathers for the church; while the other, unable to beget fathers, begets children for the church through the regeneration of the washing, but not fathers or teachers.

**75,4,3a** And how was it possible for the presbyter to appoint, when he does not have the laying on of hands for ordaining, or to say that he is equal to the bishop?

**75,4,3b** But his own contentiousness and his jealousy deceived the aforesaid Aerius.

**75,4,4a** He brings forward, to the deceiving of himself and of those who listen to him, the claim that the apostle addresses his letters to presbyters and deacons, and does not write to bishops.

**75,4,4b** And to the bishop he says, “Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which you received through the hands of the presbytery.”
